Committee: Judiciary
Sponsor: Holmes
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 02/22/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 2 as introduced adds Tianeptine to the list of Schedule II controlled substances making these drugs unlawful and persons convicted of possession, distribution, and trafficking of these substances are subject to existing criminal penalties. This bill could increase receipts to the State General Fund from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of the State General Fund, district attorneys, the Board of Pardons and Paroles, the Department of Corrections and community corrections programs by an amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by the bill and the penalties imposed.
Jim Hill, Chair
Judiciary

This bill could increase receipts to the State General Fund from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of the State General Fund, district attorneys, the Board of Pardons and Paroles, the Department of Corrections and community corrections programs by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by the bill and the penalties imposed.

Committee: Judiciary

Date: 03/31/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 2 as passed the House of Representatives adds Tianeptine to the list of Schedule II controlled substances making these drugs unlawful and persons convicted of possession, distribution, and trafficking of these substances subject to existing criminal penalties. This bill could increase receipts to the State General Fund from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of the State General Fund, district attorneys, the Board of Pardons and Paroles, the Department of Corrections and community corrections programs by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by the bill and the penalties imposed.
As amended and reported by the Committee on Judiciary, adds Delta-8-Tetrahydrocannabinol and Delta-10-Tetrahydrocannabinol to the list of Schedule II controlled substances making these drugs unlawful and persons convicted of possession, distribution, and trafficking of these substances subject to existing criminal penalties which could further increase receipts to the State General Fund from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of the State General Fund, district attorneys, the Bureau of Pardons and Paroles, the Department of Corrections and community corrections programs by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by the bill and the penalties imposed.
Tom Whatley, Chairperson
Judiciary

Committee: Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development
Sponsor: Rafferty
Analyst: Bryan Young
Date: 02/25/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 57 as passed the House of Representatives provides for the continuance of the Alabama Athletic Commission until October 1, 2023 pursuant to the Alabama Sunset Law. This bill will not otherwise affect state or local funding.
Steve Livingston, Chairperson
Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development
